title: [observability] message_not_taken clears once a later message of its session is taken, and never fires for one whose later message was taken first
prompt:
Spawn, objective 138 [observability]: an open `message_not_taken` alert clears once a later message of its session is taken. A message whose later one was taken before it fell due never fires. Today one missed marker in a resident agent's session leaves the alert open for good (agent_resident_flake #1925, open more than 2 h after the agent took later work; queue lead line "Spawn 138").

Where things stand (main 853b5460):
- A message Spawn types into a session (`input`, or a prompted `start`/`resume`) ends with its marker, `[spawn message #<id>]`. The transcript line that holds it records `message.taken` (detail `command_id`).
- `spawn_command_message` (crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql) reads a command's message from the records: `tracked`, `taken`, `due_ms`, `typed`, `ended`, `acted`, …
- The alerts step (crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs, `messages`) fires `message_not_taken` for a tracked message that no `message.taken` names past its bound (SPAWN_MESSAGE_TAKEN_SECS), its session not ended. An open one clears only when that message is taken, or when its session ends with it untaken.
- A resident agent's session never ends. When the agent works a message but its marker is missed (the line passed over, or written without the marker), it goes on to take later messages, and the alert stays open for good. That is #1925.

Read: crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_command_message`, `spawn_events_message_taken`), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`messages`, its module doc), crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs (MESSAGES_SINCE, MESSAGES_ALL), crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (SESSION_COMMANDS), rsi/scenarios/045.sh (the world and its fake engine).

Required behaviour.
- `spawn_command_message` gains `later_taken` and `later_taken_at_ms`: the first `message.taken` (by event id) in the same session whose `command_id` is greater than this message's. They are read only for a tracked message typed and not taken (`tracked`, typed, and `taken` = 0): an untyped message is behind nothing the agent took, whatever order the Bridge types in. They are null otherwise or when there is none. Another session's taking never counts.
- `message_not_taken`:
  - an open alert clears when its message is taken (as today, evidence `taken`). Otherwise, once `later_taken` is set, it clears with evidence `{"later_taken": <that command id>, "taken_at_ms": <its time>}`. Otherwise it clears at its session's end (as today);
  - a message with `later_taken` set never fires (as one taken or ended, it leaves the pending set);
  - nothing else changes: the bound, the typed and marked rules, once per message, the notice.
- The commands API (`/api/sessions/<id>/commands`, SESSION_COMMANDS) keeps its fields: it strips `later_taken` and `later_taken_at_ms` as it strips `tracked`, `due_ms`, `typed` and `ended`.
- No new record, no new event, no schema table or index. The lookup uses `spawn_events_message_taken` (session_id, command_id, id).

Polled read: the lookup is inside `spawn_command_message`, which the alerts step's MESSAGES_SINCE / MESSAGES_ALL and the commands API call per command. It runs only for a tracked message typed and not taken. sync/obj-138/138-timing.sql is a read-only SELECT that times it for every command of a window (an upper bound): the lead timed it on live (2026-11-14, upper bound): 24 h, 80 commands, 1.3–1.5 ms; 7 d, 1113 commands, 11–12 ms; through spawn_events_message_taken. Cost PASS (the lead).

Unit tests (spawn-cli, alerts.rs, on the test database):
- `a_message_not_taken_clears_when_a_later_one_is_taken`: one fires; two later ones taken before the read clear it naming the first taking (`later_taken`); a message after that one, untaken, fires and stays open; the session's end clears it (`ended`);
- `a_message_whose_later_one_was_taken_first_never_fires`;
- `a_later_taking_of_another_session_or_before_the_typing_counts_for_nothing` (rev-f R1 F1, N1): another session's later taking neither clears an open alert nor keeps one from firing; an untyped message fires though a later one of its session was taken;
- `a_message_not_taken_is_one_alert_until_taken_or_its_session_ends` (not renamed): taking the untyped one now clears it (taken 1) and the deaf one before it (later_taken = the untyped one), and the session's end then clears nothing. Its assertions change because the rule changes, and its doc comment says so.
Each rule removed alone must fail a test or the scenario. No test is renamed or dropped.

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (+16), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (+2 −1), rsi/scenarios/138.sh (new). No other open objective touches them (133 and 135, which touched schema.sql and alerts.rs, have landed: the base holds them).
The throwaway is +212 −18 on 853b5460: code and doc comments +38 −6 (schema.sql +18, alerts.rs +18 −5, fleet.rs +2 −1), tests +174 −12 (alerts.rs). rsi/scenarios/138.sh is new.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/138.sh. Black box in 045's world: a real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, the dispatcher, the alerts step) runs two ephemeral workers, late and quick, on 045's fake engine. Each worker's mode is set per agent. `take` writes what is typed into its transcript and ends the turn. `nomark` (138's own) does the same but writes the line without its marker, as a missed marker reads: never seen taken, yet the agent goes on to the next input. Inputs come from a person (`spawn submit`). SPAWN_MESSAGE_TAKEN_SECS=12.
(1) late, nomark: input A is typed and worked, and its alert opens. late takes again and input B is taken. A's alert clears within 20 s, and the clear's evidence names B (`later_taken`).
(2) late, nomark again: input C, after B, fires and is still open 10 s after it opened, because nothing later was taken.
(3) quick, nomark: input D is typed and worked without its marker (the scenario waits for the engine's nomark turn to end before switching quick back to take). quick takes again before D's bound, and input E is taken. 24 s on, D has no alert, and the records hold no alert fired for it (one fired and cleared since counts). late's C is still open: quick's takings count for nothing in late's session.
On the base (853b5460), 138.sh exits 1 at its first check: "(1) input B to late was taken after input A, and A's message_not_taken alert is [open ], not cleared within 20 s". On the throwaway:
- 138.sh passes twice; 045, 046, 047, 133 and 135 pass;
- check-clippy (spawn-cli, spawn-postgres) is clean. cargo fmt --check fails only on crates/spawn-postgres/tests/backup.rs, which fails the same on the base and is not 138's file. alerts:: passes 95 of 95, and acks, message_due, human_input and human_key pass. The test list gains the 3 names above, and none is missing.
8 mutants, each alone (mut138.py), each built from a fresh tree:
- sql-later-dropped (no lookup) and clear-dropped (no clear on later_taken) fail check (1): A stays open;
- sql-earlier-counts (an earlier message counts) fails check (1): A never fires;
- fire-not-skipped (fires though a later one was taken) fails check (3): D fired;
- any-session (another session's taking counts; rev-f R1 F1) fails check (3): late's C cleared;
- last-not-first (the last later taking, not the first; R1 F2) fails a_message_not_taken_clears_when_a_later_one_is_taken;
- untyped-counts (an untyped message counts; R1 N1) fails a_later_taking_of_another_session_or_before_the_typing_counts_for_nothing;
- fleet-strip-dropped (the commands API shows the new keys) fails each_command_reads_its_message_by_its_id.
Each fails at least one alerts:: unit test.

Verified by: the gate runs 138.sh on the candidate. After the landing, the lead reads /api/core-lines and the alerts and posts in sync that #1925 (agent_resident_flake) is cleared with `later_taken` evidence, and that no open `message_not_taken` remains for a session that has taken a later message.
rev-f reviews.
